recipes.name: Balsamic Marinated Chicken Breasts
ingredients_raw: 4 (6 ounce) skinless, boneless chicken breast halves

steps.text: Whisk together the balsamic vinegar, water, onion, red pepper flakes, garlic, salt, pepper, paprika, rosemary, parsley, chili powder, and oregano in a bowl, and pour into a resealable plastic bag. Add the chicken breasts, coat with the marinade, squeeze out excess air, and seal the bag. Marinate in the refrigerator 30 minutes to overnight.

Preheat oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). Line a baking sheet with aluminum foil, or lightly grease a broiler pan. Remove the chicken breasts from the marinade, and shake off excess. Discard the remaining marinade, and place the chicken breasts onto the baking sheet.

Bake in the preheated oven until the chicken breasts are golden brown and no longer pink in the center, 30 to 40 minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should reach 165 degrees F (74 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Balsamic Marinated Chicken Breasts
raw_recipe.description: This is a recipe I made up after eating LOADS of bland chicken breasts. Chicken is so easy to prepare and this recipe makes the meat extra tender and juicy.

review.reviewBody: This popped into my email as a new recipe and I had chicken in the fridge so I tried it last night. I'm glad I did! It was so easy to marinate during the day - pop it into the oven and you have a great weeknight meal. While it was baking I could work on the other dishes. I did not use red pepper flakes and used fresh rosemary and fresh garlic. My husband said "wow, this is good!". Make this dish!

I loved this recipe.. however I did make some changes. I used onion powder in place of dried onion, added a bit of olive oil, and used fresh minced garlic. Also, I lined the cooking sheet with cubed red potatoes, cherry tomatoes, and brussel sprouts that I covered lightly in olive oil, salt and pepper and baked before hand for 20 min at 425°. Then topped with this marinated chicken and baked the time it called for. So good!
Anything Balsamic I love and I loved your recipe. The leftover marinade I brought to a rolling boil and thickened a little for a sauce. 👍👍
I added 1/4 c. of olive oil and skipped the water. My husband really liked this. We eat a lot of chicken so glad to have a new recipe to turn to.
The amount of spices added is not enough. I doubled the rosemary, parsley, and chili powder; plus used 1 tsp oregano. This is a good balsamic marinade and will make again.

What an excellent recipe! I made this tonight for my boyfriend and it was a complete success! The only thing I did different was to only use 1/2 cup balsamic vinegar, use italian seasoning in place of the oregano, rosemary, and parsley, added fresh garlic, and a splash of OJ. Let marinate overnight, and cooked at 350 for about 30-35 minutes. The chicken was wonderfully moist, and so tasty. My bf remarked he could taste many different flavors in the chicken as well. I will definitely be making this again! Thank you for the recipe!
I marinated the chicken for a day and a half and it practically melted in my mouth! Could not get an ouch of it- next time I’ll make more and freeze the extras

I made this for the Mrs & mine weekly food prep. Cutting the chicken breast into chunks helps cut down on the cooking time and also helps keep it moist (in my opinion). It falls apart in your mouth if done right. I opted for a lower temperature (since my oven is super small). Came out amazing!
Great recipes thanks- I just not sure why you discarded the marinade. I made it in a cast iron skillet and cooked the marinade into a sauce after chicken was done

I increased dried minced onion to 1 TBS and left out the dried parsley. The wife and I both loved it. Served it with some rosemary parmesan roasted red potatoes and a salad. Will be a go to menu item for me when we have dinner guests in the future.

Looks great I have a variation I like....I keep the marinade and put the whole thing in a meatloaf pan. 350 for 30 to 35 minutes. Keeps it moist and wonderful. The marinade pretty much cooks off and leave with a clear brown fluid remaining so I know its done if its not cloudy. A few spatterings of vinegar here an dthere I drain and eat the whole chicken breast myself like a pig. A bit of Pik-a-Peppa sause and Im in heaven....

I knew when I read this recipe that I would probably not like it, and I didn’t. I cut my breast a in 1/2 and marinated 5 hours and they were very tender, but that was the only redeeming value for this recipe. I would say, we didn’t toss it, but we won’t make it again. Maybe a variation because I love all the ingredients..just not together.

I used as another review suggested Mirim instead of water. Doubled the spices/herbs (was a little too much red pepper and chili pepper), added ltsp of ground mustard , added some Worcestershire sauce. I added some 1/2 half because it became to spicy but overall was very good.
It’s a keeper. Serve with wild rice and a salad to cut the tang of the vinegar.

It is simple and easy to make. I haven't really liked chicken for the past few years. So, every now and then I'll try something new. I came across this one and I had all the ingredients. We don't like spicy hot seasonings and I don't own any of those spices. I was hoping it would turn out good. I follow the directions, left it in the frig for about an hour and put it in the oven. WOW. This was wonderful. My husband liked it too. We will be making this more as we go forward. Good eating.
Spices conflicted a bit, so omitted the chili powder. Great flavor! Have made it many times!

This is very good but I can see how the flavor profile might not hit everyone’s pallet positively. Balsamic and red wine are bold flavors and combined, might be a tad overwhelming. We in particular really enjoyed this. Marinated for nearly 10.5 hours and did on the Traeger which came out super moist and tender. If you like balsamic and red wine, try this. If leery of either or both - perhaps proceed with caution. For us, we are super glad we tried!! Thanks RUpchurch!!

Definitely going into my meal rotation. This was delicious, the chicken was SO moist and tender and the flavors were great! I made the marinade in the morning and put it in the oven around 5 so I’d say it marinated for about 6 hrs. My only change was to reduce the balsamic from 3/4 to 1/2 cup and did not add salt. My wife loved it and I will be serving this to guests.

Followed the recipe exactly and marinated in the fridge about 5 hours. Must have done something wrong because it was almost inedible. With the help of some bottled BBQ sauce , we were able to eat. It was very tender.

Very delicious! The only downside was the chicken breast was a little dry. That is my fault for not checking the chicken about 10 minutes earlier. I did use fresh onion and garlic, but that was it. Will definitely make again.
